QGraphicsView gives a proper hardware-accelerated 2D scene graph with transforms, opacity, animations, hit-testing — exactly what we need for a depth-cued tower diagram with clickable floors, lift cars, OpenClaw marker, worker density swirls.

Building our own scene engine (the QSB Scene Engine) on top of QGraphicsView keeps the data layer engine-agnostic; we can swap to Qt3D, Panda3D, or Godot later without rewriting the floor/worker/lift/openclaw renderers.
Result: a real native desktop window running TODAY, no Chrome dependency, no WebGL dependency.
risks: Not true 3D — the tower is depth-cued isometric/pseudo-3D with shading, not a Z-buffered mesh. For real perspective 3D the user must install python3-pyqt5.qt3d or pip-install Panda3D.
If the user runs this over SSH without X11 forwarding the window will not open. Health-check warns explicitly.
